$comment: Language-neutral golden vectors binding the TS capture-core disk spool (packages/capture-core/src/spool.ts) and the Hermes Python port (clients/hermes/python/src/membase_hermes/spool.py). Both test suites consume this file so the on-disk contract — capture_id hashing and the enqueue drop rules — cannot drift between languages. The file-locking/retry mechanics are per-language and intentionally NOT vectorized. Content in capture_id cases is ALREADY sanitized (sanitize itself is covered by sanitize-vectors.json), so these isolate the hash computation.

capture_id.$comment: sha256("{session_id||'unknown'}:{capture_kind}:{sanitized_content}") as lowercase hex. Verifies TS captureId and Python compute_capture_id agree byte-for-byte.

cases.content: a captured note worth keeping around
a captured note worth keeping around

enqueue_drop_rules.$comment: Given content (post-sanitize length is what matters), enqueue returns a record (keep=true) or null (keep=false). MIN_CONTENT_LENGTH=20.

cases.content: this is long enough to keep

dedupe.$comment: Enqueuing the same (session_id, capture_kind, content) twice keeps only the first; the second returns null.
